newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania army to guard buildings, roads.
newsitem.headline: Albania army to guard buildings, roads.

text.p: Albania's parliament on Sunday authorised the use of the military to guard roads and government buildings as violent protests around the Balkan state escalated.

Parliament, mostly made up of deputies of the ruling right-wing Democratic Party, voted by 96 votes in favour and just two against for the measure after two weeks of demonstrations against collapsing savings schemes.

Parliament, sitting for the first time on a Sunday since President Sali Berisha's Democrats swept to power in a 1992 general election, took the vote in an emergency session after demonstrators set scores of buildings ablaze, mainly in towns in the south.
Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu, himself attacked during a protest in the town of Lushnje on Saturday, blamed the growing crisis on what he called "extremist forces".

"It is not the mass of Albanian Socialists, but there are some Marxist extremists who have always wanted to seize power through violence," Shehu told reporters after the vote. "These are segments of the former secret police who want to profit from this moment when Albanian citizens are having financial difficulties to try to destabilise Albania."

Witnesses earlier saw two military trucks carrying about 40 soldiers arrive at the interior ministry in central Tirana. Soldiers armed with sub-machine guns were already on guard around the main Skanderbeg Square where several government buildings are sited.
